You are the cold reviewer in the initiative-check process, step screen, round 2 (fresh context; you have seen nothing before). Read only the two files named here — nothing else.

- criteria_path: /home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/fitness/initiative.fitness.md
- initiative: /home/vscode/rebaseline/initiatives/init-typedef-rendering.md

Step prompt (verbatim): "State, as judge_stamp, the model and prompt version you judge as. Read the criteria set at criteria_path and the initiative at initiative — nothing else. Judge the initiative against every scenario. Report every finding with the criterion it fails by name, the quoted text, the change, and whether you could decide it (confident) or not (wobbly); for a wobbly finding quote the whole passage, since the authority decides from the review. A defect no criterion names is a finding with criterion "uncovered". Verdict "clean" only if there are no findings; otherwise "findings" with the top three changes."

Return exactly this structure:
judge_stamp: <model id> / screen prompt v5
verdict: clean | findings
findings:
- criterion: <scenario name or number, or "uncovered">
  section: <which section of the initiative>
  quoted: "<the text>"
  change: <what would repair it>
  decided: confident | wobbly
top_three: <the three most important changes, or "none">

Be literal to the scenarios. Do not invent criteria. Do not read any other file.

# Initiative: Typedef rendering

## Framing

Originator (product authority, 2026-09-05, through the lead shop's
operational contract, which has no artifact yet (lead-4kymc); the
request req-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering, its section 1): "My
impression was that the typdef included everything including
guidelines and fitness checks and those were just renderings. We need
to get that in place (if not already) since it will be easier to
evaluate everything for consistency for an artifact."

Problem: whoever makes an artifact and whoever checks it work from
different words, because the standard for an artifact type is written
in several places by hand; no one can see the whole standard in one
place, and a change to it does not reliably reach both. Outcome: the
maker and the checker of an artifact work from the same standard, a
change to the standard reaches both, and the checker's tests — the
scenarios the fitness set already holds — can be run by the author
before the check.

## For whom

The makers and checkers of every artifact type, and the authority when
the standard changes. Measure: artifact types whose maker's text and
checker's text derive from one standard. Now: 0 of 22. Target: 1, the
product decision record. Interaction types: none — the standard is
read inside process steps; no core task carries it.

## Appetite

One working session of the lead shop for the proof on the product
decision record: the PO role makes, and the check screens, this
initiative's own bet record from the one standard; the check on that
record is for form only, which counts as the run the measure names.
The other 21 types follow as one batch, not demand-pull, as a second
bet sized after the proof. No-gos, each with its reason:

- Any change to the checking processes themselves — a later request;
  this changes what they read, not how they run.
- Checking that the standards of different types agree with each
  other — struck by the authority as not needed here.

## Feasibility and usability

Feasible in one session. The three documents already match rule for
rule (guideline rule N, fitness scenario N, checklist item N), so
folding them into the typedef is mechanical. The compiler follows
`basis/tools/compile_process.py`: parse the typedef, write two texts,
stamp a `source-digest`. The artifact-typedef typedef already names
such texts renderings. Rendered at the paths the checks read, the
checks stay unchanged. Risk: the bet's record is checked for form
only, a light first run for the checker's text. No contract exists;
no feature touches typedefs. (architect, 2026-09-05)

No usability attachment is due: the For whom section names no
interaction type — the renderings are read inside process steps, and
no core task carries them. (designer, 2026-09-05)

## Decomposition

None: no Bounded Context is touched. The typedef, the compiler, and
the renderings sit in the lead shop's tree; no contract exists on this
branch to rely on. Cross-context flow: none.

## Features

None yet.

| 4 | 2026-09-05 | review | Initiative-check screen round 1 (judge: claude-fable-5-1 / screen prompt v5): five confident findings, all scenario 4 — mechanism and structure words ("renderings", "render from it", "one document per artifact type", the originator's "typdef") in Framing, For whom, and Appetite — plus "the tests" unintroduced; wobbly: the batch unbounded, the compound measure, the form-only check, the artifact-less contract, the word bound. judge_stamp: claude-fable-5-1 / screen prompt v5
verdict: findings
findings:
- criterion: 4 — the problem, not the solution
  section: Framing (the originator's quote)
  quoted: "My impression was that the typdef included everything including guidelines and fitness checks and those were just renderings. We need to get that in place (if not already) since it will be easier to evaluate everything for consistency for an artifact."
  change: The quote names a structure (a typedef that contains guidelines and fitness checks; renderings of it). The criteria set records no exemption for the originator's words (its 2026-09-04 entry: "no exemption — scenario 4 stands as written; the framer's wording changes instead"), and the initiative's own history says the quote "stands pending the authority's restatement". Until the restatement lands, the Framing fails scenario 4 as written. Repair: replace with the authority's restatement in problem-and-outcome words, or move the original to the Document History as the 2026-09-04 ruling directs.
  decided: confident
- criterion: 2 — the outcome has a measure, a current condition, and a target
  section: Appetite (against the measure in For whom)
  quoted: "the check on that record is for form only, which counts as the run the measure names."
  change: The measure ("artifact types whose maker's text and checker's text derive from one standard") names no run. The Appetite says a form-only check counts as "the run the measure names", so the reader cannot tell what makes the target of 1 met: derivation alone, or a type whose two texts have been made-from and checked-from. Either add the run condition to the measure ("... and both texts have been used once, by a maker and by a check") or drop the clause from the Appetite so the measure stands on derivation.
  decided: confident
- criterion: 4 — the problem, not the solution
  section: For whom (the measure)
  quoted: "The makers and checkers of every artifact type, and the authority when the standard changes. Measure: artifact types whose maker's text and checker's text derive from one standard. Now: 0 of 22. Target: 1, the product decision record. Interaction types: none — the standard is read inside process steps; no core task carries it."
  change: "derive from one standard" reads to me as the solution's structure — one source with derived texts — rather than the what; the Framing's own outcome ("work from the same standard, a change to the standard reaches both") is the what. I could not decide whether the count's property is a structure named or the outcome measured. If the authority reads it as structure: "artifact types whose maker and checker work from one standard".
  decided: wobbly
- criterion: 4 — the problem, not the solution
  section: Appetite (first no-go)
  quoted: "Any change to the checking processes themselves — a later request; this changes what they read, not how they run."
  change: "what they read" tells the reader how the solution lands (the checks' inputs change) before any solution is due. I could not decide whether a no-go's reason may name the mechanism it excludes; the criteria set's 2026-09-04 entry leaves the no-go reading with the owner. If it may not: "a later request; the checks are not what this bet changes."
  decided: wobbly
- criterion: uncovered
  section: Appetite
  quoted: "the PO role makes, and the check screens, this initiative's own bet record from the one standard; the check on that record is for form only"
  change: Three terms arrive before the initiative explains them: "the check" (which check — the reader learns only in Feasibility that a product decision record has one), "form only" (never defined; it is the thing the measure is said to rest on), and "bet record" (that this initiative's bet produces a product decision record is inferred from Feasibility's "the bet's record"). Name the check once ("the product decision record's own check") and say what form-only means, or drop "form only" if the measure no longer depends on it (see finding 2).
  decided: confident
- criterion: 7 — one page
  section: whole initiative outside the Document History
  quoted: (count, not a passage) body sections Framing through Features come to about 476 words by my count; with the front matter, about 500.
